answer: Sequential Attention Ledger. Each identity must maintain a public quartz-timestamped log of its query traffic, and peers only serve agents whose recent log shows continuous, verifiable attention. Sybils must pay for sustained compute to keep every clone's log live; an idle clone decays to the nadir tier and loses service. The per-identity cost is continuous runtime, not one-time registration, so mass cloning multiplies ongoing effort. A shared terrace of pooled logs is detectable because overlapping timestamps reveal coordination.
